title: Apply to downgrade a driver licence
summary: This page provides information on how to apply to downgrade your driver licence at a Service NSW Centre.
intro:
You may need to or want to downgrade your licence due to:

You can downgrade your licence at a Service NSW Centre.
who_can_apply: Must be able to visit a Service NSW Centre to submit the application.
what_you_need: Your current licence, or proof of identity if the licence is unavailable.
Evidence of why you need to downgrade (if involuntary), such as your contact lenses or glasses.

how_to_steps.text: Make sure you have all your documentation and any additional items (if applicable).
Visit a service centre and submit your application.

fees:
Depending on the reason for the licence downgrade you may have to pay a fee.

At most service centre locations, you can pay by EFTPOS, credit or debit card – Mastercard, Visa, American Express or UnionPay.

Not all service centre locations accept cash. Check the list of locations where cash is not accepted before you visit.

more_info.text: Renewal notices are posted generally within 6 weeks before the card's expiry date.
For driver licence renewals or applications, a receipt is provided that allows you to drive until the card arrives in the post. The receipt is valid for 2 months.

faqs.q: Where can I apply to downgrade my licence?
faqs.a: You can downgrade your licence at a Service NSW Centre.

faqs.q: What do I need to bring when I apply?
faqs.a: You need your current licence (or proof of identity if the licence is unavailable), your concession card details (if applicable), and evidence of why you need to downgrade (if involuntary).

faqs.q: How do I pay for the licence downgrade?
faqs.a: You can pay by EFTPOS, credit or debit card (Mastercard, Visa, American Express, or UnionPay) at most service centre locations. Note that not all locations accept cash.
